notes: Access: robots.txt (https://www.iittala.com/robots.txt) checked first, no Claude-specific disallow, only cart/checkout/search/locale-duplicate paths blocked. Tier-1 HTTP (curl) fetch of homepage and the site's own sitemap.xml (https://www.iittala.com/en-gb/sitemap.xml, 1206 URLs) worked but the storefront is a Sitecore/Coveo client-rendered React app (initial HTML has no product grid or counts, only hydration shells) so exact qty required Tier-2 Playwright rendering (networkidle + scroll) per company access-tier rules; no Claude-in-Chrome needed. Main nav (Tableware/Home Decor/Collections/Gifts/Universe) currently shows no seasonal top-level item (checked live rendered menu + full href crawl of homepage, 217 unique links) because the crawl date (2026-09-04) is off-season, but the sitemap.xml exposes a full /christmas/ URL branch plus Easter/Mother's/Father's/Valentine's 'gifts by occasion' pages that remain live (HTTP 200) year-round even though delinked from the visible top nav. Cross-checked the Finnish home-market sitemap (fi-fi/sitemap.xml) and it mirrors the same taxonomy 1:1 (joulu=Christmas with identical sub-slugs, paasiaiskoristeet=Easter Decorations, aitienpaiva/isanpaiva/ystavanpaiva = Mother's/Father's/Valentine's Day gifts) confirming no additional local-language-only festival exists (no Halloween, Diwali, Thanksgiving, New Year, or Indian-festival branch on either market). Used en-gb (the locale the site itself defaults new sessions to, confirmed via Set-Cookie: fiskarsiittala#country=en / shell#lang=en on a plain root fetch) for the verified links and qty. For every candidate under /christmas/, /home-decor/decorative-objects/, and /gifts/gifts-by-occasion/ I rendered the live page and used the presence of the site's own 'Filter / Sorting / Most popular / N results' PLP widget as the discriminator between a genuine filterable category (included) and a curated editorial/gift-guide or 'coming soon' landing page (excluded), per the shared PLP-vs-marketing-page rule. INCLUDED: Christmas (root, grouping node - links to child hub pages, no own product grid) > Christmas Decorations (grouping node - a themed landing page with multiple product carousels but no own Filter/count widget) > Silver Decorations (genuine PLP, 13 results); Christmas > Christmas Gifts (grouping node - same landing-page pattern) > Christmas Gifts for Her (150 results), Christmas Gifts for Him (123 results), Christmas Gifts for Dad (101 results), Christmas Gifts for Mom (124 results), Christmas Gifts for Couples (123 results), Secret Santa Gifts (81 results) - each confirmed with its own Filter/Sorting/results widget and product grid; Easter > Easter Decorations (27 results, breadcrumb Home>Home Decor>Decorative objects>Easter Decorations, page title/copy explicitly Easter-themed even though nested under the normal Home Decor tree - included per the overlap rule since the site itself labels it Easter); Mother's Day > Mother's Day Gifts (64 results, breadcrumb Home>Gifts>Gifts by occasion>Mother's Day Gifts, genuine Filter/Sort/count PLP). EXCLUDED after investigation: Christmas Table Setting (/christmas/christmas-table-setting) - themed landing page with several curated product carousels (red styling, Teema cherry, holiday table) but no own Filter/Sort/count widget and no further sitemap child of its own, so it is neither a leaf PLP nor a grouping parent - a pure marketing/inspiration page; Advent Calendars (/christmas/advent-calendars) - 'COMING SOON: ADVENT CALENDARS 2026' page with zero products, no grid, no count; Valentine's Day Gifts (/gifts/gifts-by-occasion/valentines-day-gifts) and Father's Day Gifts (/gifts/gifts-by-occasion/fathers-day-gifts) - both rendered and re-checked with full scroll/networkidle wait, confirmed (unlike Mother's Day Gifts) they carry no Filter/Sorting/results widget, just a small curated 'gift ideas' selection (~14-32 tiles, no total count exposed) - editorial gift-guide pages, not genuine filterable categories; Black Week (/black-week) - page title is literally 'Black Friday Sale', a discount campaign page, explicitly excluded per the Sale-page rule. No Halloween, Diwali, Thanksgiving, New Year, or any Indian-festival category exists anywhere in nav, mega-menu, or either market's sitemap - confirmed absent, not merely unsearched.
